Verdict

Reviewed 20 Oct 2026 · next 18 Apr 2027

Reasonable API and active, but ESM-only, one dependency, 472 KB installed, no type declarations and no publish workflow. Hold unless a specific feature is needed.

Current Reviewed version 6.0.9 Requirement: Deep merge of nested configuration objects

Reasoning

  1. One runtime dependency (is-what) and a 472 KB install, the largest of the candidates.
  2. No published type declarations despite being written in TypeScript.
  3. Only a test workflow exists; publishing is manual and there is no provenance.
  4. Safe against CVE-2026-93753; replaces arrays rather than concatenating.

Caveats

  • ESM-only, so CommonJS consumers cannot use it without a dynamic import.
  • Array replacement semantics differ from the rest of the field.

Decision context

Approved

@fastify/deepmerge is the primary choice for Deep merge of nested configuration objects. This package is classified as On hold.

Adopt @fastify/deepmerge as the primary implementation: it is the only candidate that combines OIDC trusted publishing, SLSA provenance, zero runtime dependencies, bundled types, active maintenance and immunity to CVE-2026-93753. deepmerge-ts is approved as the fallback for cyclic inputs or Map/Set merging, at the cost of a long-lived NPM_TOKEN in its release pipeline. deepmerge is dropped because the vulnerability has no upstream fix and is invisible to npm audit. ts-deepmerge, merge-deep, lodash.merge, @corex/deepmerge, deep-extend and the CVE-fork packages are rejected; defu, merge-anything and @75lb/deep-merge remain on hold and are not approved for this requirement.
